versionBoundary: Exact saved official rust-v0.156.1 sources identified by tag URL and byte hash. This does not pin a runtime binary, verify a newly installed process, or establish behavior for other versions.
conclusion: The researched version-checked generic official write route is a concrete implementation candidate. The dedicated skills writer has source-visible representation and result-reporting risks. No global external-process lock is proposed as a prerequisite or claimed by this review.

findings.classification: source-visible path; not reproduced by CLI/API here
findings.fact: set_skill_config only treats skills.config as ArrayOfTables. For an existing inline array, enabled=false replaces it with an empty ArrayOfTables before inserting the target rule, while enabled=true returns without mutation. The three inspected upstream examples use ArrayOfTables.
findings.implication: Do not blindly use the dedicated writer on unknown representation or treat a successful response as preservation of unrelated rules.

findings.fact: skills_config_write_response_inner returns effective_enabled: enabled after apply/cache invalidation. It does not reload the effective state. Enabling removes the first matching override rather than writing an explicit true; another matching name/path or higher SessionFlags rule can still disable the skill.
findings.implication: Report desired preference, persistence and effective list result separately; echoed effectiveEnabled is not acceptance evidence.

findings.classification: direct source fact plus bounded race inference
findings.fact: config/value/write validates only the allowed user path and compares expectedVersion with the loaded active User layer before persistence. The later ConfigEditsBuilder rereads TOML and applies the exact key edit without a second atomic version check. Returned version/status use calculated updated_layers, not a postwrite filesystem reread. Same-server global config serialization does not cover external writers.
findings.implication: Reject stale prechecks; after dispatch use explicit readback to determine observed outcome. Do not claim global CAS or blindly retry/restore prior config after unknown outcome.

findings.classification: direct source fact; future interoperability risk not experimentally verified
findings.fact: The generic writer represents TOML arrays using Value::Array and table elements using InlineTable. Writing skills.config through that route can therefore produce the representation rejected by the dedicated writer above.
findings.implication: Do not automatically switch/fallback to skills/config/write. Owned interoperability verification must cover subsequent dedicated edits as well as immediate generic-write preservation.

findings.fact: The precise methods are config/read with includeLayers and explicit cwd, followed after a confirmed edit by fresh config/read and skills/list with the exact original cwd and forceReload. No config/list method is used by this design. skills/list reloads configuration for each cwd and returns current skills/errors.
findings.implication: Partial/errors, missing target, state mismatch or different identity do not count as effective success; a separate management process report does not prove adoption by an existing ACP conversation.

candidate.scope: One explicit reversible user-layer preference for a currently discovered non-plugin user/repo skill, selected by exact private path rather than display name or ordinal.
sequence: Fresh official config/read(includeLayers=true,cwd=exact selected cwd), retaining only bounded private User-layer path/version and complete skills.config array.
Show the target and user-layer scope, then consume one exact-owner confirmation. Preserve every non-target rule and order; reject ambiguity instead of silently normalizing.
Official config/value/write(keyPath=skills.config,mergeStrategy=replace,filePath=exact User layer,expectedVersion=fresh version) with the complete intended array.
Fresh config/read verifies the intended user-layer change and preservation, then skills/list(forceReload=true,cwds=[exact cwd]) checks the same target and effective enabled state.
candidate.privateData: config/read may return unrelated sensitive configuration. Bound and validate it inside the backend, publish only the minimal allowed result, and do not log raw configuration or private skill paths.
candidate.unknownOutcome: After possible write dispatch, cancellation/timeout/lost response is unknown, not not-written. Preserve exact request ownership, finish owned process cleanup and offer explicit readback without automatic mutation retry or rollback.
candidate.nextVerification: Use only self-owned controlled configuration to compare ArrayOfTables and inline arrays, duplicates/name precedence, stale version rejection, postcheck external drift and full semantic preservation. This is an implementation prerequisite for the selected candidate, not evidence of already passing management.

boundaries: No official mutation, config/account experiment, native GUI, live tools, model request or Cargo execution was performed.
Readback would establish configuration and the management process report only; it cannot establish current model/tool use or automatic reload of separate conversations.
Official normal startup may maintain its own state; no zero-write/no-background-network guarantee is inferred.
Source-tag-specific limitations must remain explicit if the installed official surface differs.
P40/P41 completion, broader scope/install/login/diagnostics, other Agents and Windows are not implied.

requestRoutes.supports: Official method routes, declared in-process config serialization; OAuth login/reload/status routes, no dedicated MCP OAuth cancel found in this registry.

skillsProcessor.supports: Exact selector validation; user-home writer; echoes requested enabled after persistence/cache invalidation. List reloads config per cwd.

configEdit.supports: Whole-map MCP edits; skill selector shape/mutation; symlink-resolved user config read-edit-write and blocking task.

configEditTests.supports: Upstream authored examples cover array-of-table path/name disable and removal on enable; not executed here.

atomicWrite.supports: Symlink resolution and sibling NamedTempFile write/persist; no fsync or external compare-and-swap in this function.

skillsRules.supports: Rule types; ordered path/name matching; only User/SessionFlags for per-skill rules; bundled availability separate.

configDto.supports: Config read/layers/version; write exact fields, statuses and errors; batch reload option.

configService.supports: Only user layer writable; expectedVersion checked before persistence; validation/overridden response; key parsing; null clears; array serialization.

configCredentialEdits.supports: Generic exact-key edit produces SetPath/ClearPath after semantic merge.
